comparison: Perfect overlap on physiological measurements (C47-C51). Both evaluations support these basic characterization findings about body weight, energy intake, and metabolic effects across fasting regimens.

Both address clock gene analysis (C87) with uncertainty. OpenEval notes lack of statistical detail and limited protein quantification, while peer review questions the rationale for fasting timing and its circadian implications.

Both evaluate Western blot validation (C116). OpenEval supports the orthogonal validation, while peer review raises major concerns about poor image quality, directly challenging the reliability of this validation.

Both address multi-omics integration and post-transcriptional regulation (C79-C83). OpenEval supports the findings with correlation analysis, while peer review acknowledges the observation of transcript-protein differences as interesting.
Both evaluate functional cardiac assessment (C117-C119, C10, C40). Both support the dobutamine stress test findings demonstrating improved cardiac function with intermittent fasting.

Both address duration-dependent effects and overall conclusions (C6-C9, C38-C39). Both support the finding that different fasting durations lead to distinct cardiac changes, though peer review focuses on the general principle while OpenEval evaluates broader conclusions.

Both evaluate phosphoproteomics methodology and quality (C104-C109). OpenEval supports the comprehensive approach with quality metrics, while peer review acknowledges solid technical execution without specific criticism of phosphoproteomics.

Both address proteomics findings about enzyme changes (C52-C56). OpenEval supports the hierarchical effects and enzyme quantification, while peer review challenges the specific claim that one-third of differentially expressed proteins were metabolic enzymes.

Both evaluate kinase activity inference from phosphoproteomics (C110-C113, C115). OpenEval supports the kinase motif enrichment analysis, while peer review questions the methodology for generating the kinase list.

Both evaluate experimental design and multi-omics approach (C4-C5, C36-C37, C52). Both support the technical execution, with peer review explicitly praising the solid technical aspects and novel multi-omics approach.

Both address epigenetic changes claims (C74-C76). OpenEval supports the progression to epigenetic changes in EOD based on pathway enrichment, while peer review explicitly challenges this as unsupported since chromatin or gene expression were not directly measured.

Both address metabolic pathway changes (C57-C58, C61, C69). OpenEval supports specific enzyme changes with statistical thresholds, while peer review accepts these as part of the proteomics dataset consistent with fasting responses.
Both evaluate kinase findings (C62-C63). OpenEval supports pathway-level kinase changes with FDR<0.05, while peer review questions the methodology for generating the kinase list in Figure 1B.

Both address structural protein changes (C70-C71). OpenEval supports the regimen-specific functional transitions from structural to metabolic changes, while peer review accepts these as descriptive findings without specific concerns.

Both evaluate apolipoprotein findings (C93, C55). OpenEval supports the network analysis identifying apolipoprotein changes, while peer review questions whether these reflect myocardial tissue changes or systemic effects contaminating cardiac tissue.
Minimal overlap on pathway findings (C61, C69). OpenEval supports pathway-level changes with statistical rigor, while peer review accepts metabolic pathway findings as part of the dataset.
Minimal overlap on structural changes (C64-C65). OpenEval supports regimen-specific pathway changes, while peer review accepts structural protein findings without specific challenge.

OpenEval evaluates association network analysis and mitochondrial protein enrichment (C100-C103) using IMAHP methodology. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific network analysis claims.
OpenEval evaluates literature context and study rationale (C1-C2, C11-C35). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers did not specifically assess the background claims.

OpenEval evaluates discussion claims contextualizing results (C120-C135). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on primary findings rather than discussion contextualization.
